Article Title: Google CEO Sundar Pichai responds to Sam Altman’s ‘fend Google off’ remark, asks: ‘Are you bolting agents onto ChatGPT, or …’
Article Text:
Flipping the ‘Bolt-On’ question back to OpenAI

Pichai implies ‘winning means both adapting and building new’

Alphabet and Google CEO Sundar Pichai has pushed back against claims made by OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman , rejecting the notion that Google is merely retrofitting artificial intelligence (AI) into legacy products rather than developing authentic, AI-first systems. While acknowledging the tough competition, Pichai said that the company has been making AI systems and tools from ground up as well as refining products. The debate stems from comments by Altman regarding competition between the two tech powerhouses, where the OpenAI leader argued that his company builds AI-native applications while implying that Google simply “bolts” machine learning capabilities onto its existing software suite.“First of all, it’s a very dynamic moment. We are all pushing each other. OpenAI has pushed us as a company too. This is not just we are doing something to them. Far from it,” Pichai offered a candid response, emphasising that the intense technological race is driving innovation across the board.“In the AI moment, all of us have to respond with varying levels of urgency at any given moment in time,” he added.Pichai challenged the idea that Google lacks ground-up AI platforms, citing the direct development of the standalone Gemini app as evidence of ground-up product design.He then turned the exact same design critique back toward OpenAI, questioning how ChatGPT itself handles the rapid evolution toward autonomous software agents.“We are constantly building new products as well. Gemini was built from the ground up as a product—the Gemini app I’m talking about,” Pichai noted, asking, “Or tomorrow, as all of us are adapting to agents, are you bolting agents onto ChatGPT, or are they building it natively? How would you think about that? You can always flip these questions back.”Rather than getting trapped in industry labels over what qualifies as “native” versus “integrated,” Pichai explained that successfully navigating the generative AI shift requires deploying both strategies simultaneously. The ultimate goal, he argued, is to deliver standout user experiences that perform and win in the real world.“I don’t think of it that way. I think of it as you want to build world-class product experiences that are AI-native and they are winning. Some of it is adapting products, some of it is rethinking new experiences. They will all be part of how you approach this moment,” Pichai explained.
Article Summary: Pichai implies ‘winning means both adapting and building new’ Google CEO Sundar Pichai has pushed back against claims made by OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman. Altman argued that his company builds AI-native applications while implying that Google simply “bolts” machine learning capabilities onto existing software suite.

Article Title: In 2021, a plant grower posted photos of giant water lilies in Colombia on Instagram; the pictures led researchers to a new species with less than 100 plants on Earth
Article Text:
Representative Image

How an Instagram post led to the water lily expedition

Why Victoria Colombiana species of water lilies are at risk

An Instagram post revealed an unknown giant water lily. In December 2021, Colorado carnivorous plant grower Jeremiah Harris shared photos of giant water lilies growing in Colombia’s Inírida River and identified them as Victoria Amazonica. However, water lily expert Carlos Magdalena noticed that no known Victoria species had been recorded in that part of the upper Orinoco basin. He suspected the photographs showed a previously undescribed species and used satellite imagery to search the Inírida River and its surrounding lakes, confirming the plants' presence.Magdalena and his colleagues then conducted a five-day expedition with members of local Indigenous communities. Their research eventually led to the formal description of a new species, Victoria Colombiana.After seeing Harris’ photographs, Magdalena used satellite images to examine the Inírida River and nearby lakes. The plants’ leaves were large enough to identify from space, confirming that giant water lilies were growing in the area.A research team later travelled to Inírida for a five-day expedition. It included members of the Atabapo River Indigenous reserves, including one participant who remembered seeing the plants in childhood.The search initially found only two lilies, neither with a flower. That prevented the researchers from making a reliable comparison because flower structures help botanists distinguish between closely related species.On the expedition’s final night, boat captain Gustavo Melo, a member of the Indigenous Tucano community, told the researchers about another location. At 1 a.m., he led them to a small lake where they found five additional plants, including one in bloom. The team collected the material it needed before returning for a 9 a.m. flight to Bogotá.“This is one of those extraordinary stories where indigenous and horticultural knowledge, with the help of social media and technology, came together to uncover a truly extraordinary botanical achievement,” Magdalena said in a statement.The collected flower and other plant material allowed researchers to distinguish the Inírida lilies from previously recognised members of the genus. Researchers published the findings in the scientific journal Phytotaxa, where they formally described the plant as Victoria Colombiana. The same study recognised another species, Victoria Mattogrossensis, from South America’s Pantanal region.Researchers estimate that just 30 to 50 Victoria Colombiana plants remain in the wild. The species is known only from a limited area, where changing water conditions and other environmental pressures could affect its survival. The team is working to have it classified as Critically Endangered on the IUCN Red List.“Now that we know this water lily exists, our responsibility is to understand it better and protect it. With so many plants in the wild threatened with extinction, we simply cannot wait any longer to take action,” Magdalena added.Researchers are considering establishing a naturalised population in a more accessible lake within Indigenous territory. They also hope to cultivate the species at the Bogotá Botanical Garden so researchers can study and protect it outside its known habitat. The Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew says it is even developing the conservation plans for these water lilies with local indigenous communities.
Article Summary: A Colorado carnivorous plant grower shared photos of giant water lilies growing in Colombia’s Inírida River and identified them as Victoria Amazonica. Water lily expert Carlos Magdalena noticed that no known Victoria species had been recorded in that part of the upper Orinoco basin. He suspected the photographs showed a previously undescribed species and used satellite imagery to search the river and its surrounding lakes. A research team then conducted a five-day expedition with members of local Indigenous communities. Their research led to the formal description of a new species, Victoria Colombiana.

Article Title: Rocket Mortgage founder Dan Gilbert turns his $1 billion Detroit redevelopment commitment into a nonprofit pledge; he will take no profits as the $2.2 billion project remakes Renaissance Center and 35
Article Text:
Dan Gilbert

Zero profit, no repayment: How the structure operates

A Philanthropic Shift Rather Than New Capital

Billionaire Rocket Mortgage founder Dan Gilbert is directing a massive $1 billion financial pledge toward the redevelopment of Detroit’s iconic Renaissance Center and the surrounding east riverfront through a newly formed nonprofit organisation. As per the official announcement, this philanthropic gift is believed to be the largest contribution to a non-profit redevelopment initiative in the history of American cities. Gilbert and his companies will receive no profits from the redevelopment of the Renaissance Center and 35-acre waterfront district. Gilbert's contribution will not be repaid.Under the structure, the nonprofit entity will hold full ownership of the real estate and channel any future financial surplus straight back into community initiatives. The move alters the ownership framework and beneficiaries of the broader $2.2 billion redevelopment plan, which is currently seeking roughly $548 million in public support.Gilbert’s $1 billion commitment will not be repaid, and neither Gilbert nor any of his affiliated commercial companies will take profits from the project. As per the key operational details of the arrangement, the entity, registered as a 501(c)(4) social welfare organisation, will own, build out and manage the RenCen complex and its adjacent 35-acre riverfront district.Gilbert’s primary real estate firm, Bedrock, will handle comprehensive project management services entirely free of charge. Moreover, incoming revenue will be prioritised to settle day-to-day operating costs, service outstanding debt, fund reserve accounts, and cover ongoing property reinvestment. Any remaining financial surplus will be deployed directly for broader community benefits.The inaugural board will feature Rev. Wendell Anthony, president of the Detroit branch of the NAACP, alongside former Rocket Companies CEO Bill Emerson.Gilbert stated that the nonprofit will remain dedicated to the project’s overarching community mission “in perpetuity.”Gilbert had previously earmarked roughly $1 billion for the riverfront initiative through Bedrock as a private commercial commitment. The newly revealed blueprint converts that planned private investment into a philanthropic gift, rather than injecting fresh, additional capital on top of the original target."Dan's contribution is purely a gift — not even tax-deductible — that he can't get a penny of it back," Bedrock CEO Jared Fleisher told Axios.Fleisher emphasized that while Gilbert’s contribution has become a charitable pledge, the proposed $548 million in public incentives remains essential to make the $2.2 billion development financially feasible.Long known as the global corporate headquarters of General Motors, the Renaissance Center has seen its occupancy dwindle substantially in recent years, with project developers describing the aging complex as increasingly obsolete.As part of the transformation blueprint, major physical overhauls will include demolishing two of the existing RenCen office towers, converting remaining sections of the high-rise towers into modern housing units and flexible office spaces, and replacing expansive surface parking lots with a walkable waterfront district featuring public parks, entertainment hubs and open civic spaces.
Article Summary: Rocket Mortgage founder Dan Gilbert is directing a massive $1 billion financial pledge toward the redevelopment of Detroit’s iconic Renaissance Center and the surrounding east riverfront. As per the official announcement, this philanthropic gift is believed to be the largest contribution to a non-profit redevelopment initiative in the history of American cities. Gilbert and his companies will receive no profits from the redevelopment.

Article Title: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in a new directive to American troops: You cannot use …
Article Text:
US defense secretary Pete Hegseth (Pic credit: AP)

“This prohibition applies whether the transaction is informed by classified or unclassified information,”

Why the Pentagon considers these bets a security risk

“Our enemies watch movements in these markets,”

“When an American Service member, intelligence professional, or other Department civilian engages in a financial transaction on a military outcome, they create a signal.”

“Beyond operational security, financial stakes can warp judgment. A logistician with money riding on a strike date has an interest in that date. An analyst with a position on an outcome has an interest in that outcome,”

US soldier’s alleged $409,881 profit preceded the directive

Pete Hegseth has barred US military personnel from using non-public information to bet on military events. According to the AP, the order applies to service members, intelligence staff and Pentagon civilian employees. It covers regular online betting services and prediction markets such as Polymarket and Kalshi, where users put money on whether an event will happen. Anyone who breaks the rule could face workplace punishment or criminal charges under federal or military law.Hegseth wrote in the memorandum. He said unusual betting activity could warn foreign intelligence services about planned US operations, including possible targets and attack dates. The Pentagon said it had no further information to share beyond the memo, which CBS News first reported.Hegseth wrote.Prediction-market prices change as users place trades, meaning a surge in bets from people with access to military information could indicate that an operation is approaching.The memo warns that adversaries could examine that activity to anticipate American targets, troop movements or the timing of an attack. Hegseth also said personal financial interests could affect how personnel perform their duties.he wrote in the memo.The order follows the April arrest of Master Sgt. Gannon Ken Van Dyke, a 38-year-old Special Forces soldier accused of using classified information about the operation to capture then-Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro.Federal prosecutors allege that Van Dyke placed more than $32,500 in bets between December 30 and January 2, with most of the trades occurring hours before missiles struck Caracas. He allegedly made approximately $409,881 through Polymarket contracts connected to Maduro’s removal and American military action in Venezuela. The allegations have not been proven in court. The Justice Department said the trades were based on classified details about the operation’s timing.Concerns about government-linked betting extend beyond the military. The White House previously warned staff against trading with private information after newly created Polymarket accounts made well-timed bets before a US-Iran ceasefire announcement. Kalshi also suspended and fined three congressional candidates who wagered on their own election results.
Article Summary: US defense secretary Pete Hegseth has barred US military personnel from using non-public information to bet on military events. Order applies to service members, intelligence staff and Pentagon civilian employees. Anyone who breaks the rule could face workplace punishment or criminal charges.

Article Title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang backed a Seattle lab with nearly 7 million GPU hours; its new AI model designs proteins up to 10 times faster and helps tackle pollution
Article Text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang gives AI computing power nearly 7 million GPU hours to Seattle Lab

The Jensen and Lori Huang Foundation, co-founded by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his wife Lori recently provided the UW Medicine Institute for Protein Design (IPD) with a transformational computing grant totaling nearly 7 million GPU hours. The lab recently introduced RFD4-Proteina, an open, generative model co-developed by IPD and Nvidia. The model is claimed to design proteins up to 10 times faster and uses biomolecular reasoning to improve how well scientists can design new proteins with specific functions.Making RFD4-Proteina open will allow scientists around the world to build on its capabilities, explore more potential protein designs and move promising drug candidates into laboratory testing faster.“RFD4-Proteina will open the door to new solutions in medicine, sustainability, materials and biotechnology,” said David Baker, IPD director and professor of biochemistry at the University of Washington School of Medicine.Earlier this month, the Jensen and Lori Huang Foundation, granted totaling nearly 7 million hours of compute time, will accelerate the IPD’s development of open-source AI models for protein design.The models will enable the creation of molecules with applications in medicine, technology and sustainability.The in-kind grant provided access to graphics processing units. These specialized AI computing systems will cut algorithm learning and evaluation time from months to days. It will help IPD scientists solve complex protein-design problems in such areas as precision cancer therapeutics, durable vaccines, currently untreatable diseases and new enzymes that degrade environmental toxins like long-lasting hazardous chemicals and plastics. The compute power is provided through the Huang Foundation's partnership with CoreWeave using NVIDIA graphics processing units, or GPUs.“Most of the most important medicines of the future will come from proteins that have never existed," said Jensen Huang, co-president of the Huang Foundation. "For David Baker and the Institute for Protein Design, this path means training AI on tens of millions of molecular structures, learning from virtual experiments, and finding novel protein designs that have eluded nature. The Huang Foundation is providing researchers the compute to expand the frontiers of medicine, while ensuring that the resulting models, data, and tools are openly available to all. "
Article Summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang gives AI computing power nearly 7 million GPU hours to Seattle Lab. The grant will accelerate the IPD’s development of open-source AI models for protein design. The models will enable the creation of molecules with applications in medicine, technology and sustainability.

Article Title: Michael and Susan Dell's foundation backs free skills training in Texas; a 2026 update reports that 78% of Skillpoint Alliance graduates find jobs and average monthly earnings reach $3,600
Article Text:
Michael and Susan Dell

How the training works

Industry certifications and job placement support

Addressing Texas' skilled worker shortage

Expansion planned across Central Texas

The philanthropic organisation founded by Michael Dell and Susan Dell has spotlighted the growing impact of free skilled-trades training in Texas, reporting that a large majority of participants secure employment shortly after completing the programme. According to a 2026 update from the Michael & Susan Dell Foundation, 78% of graduates from Skillpoint Alliance find jobs after completing their training, while graduates earn an average of $3,600 per month and increase their earnings by an average of 150%.Skillpoint’s pitch is speed and a direct link to employers. Traditional training programmes, the foundation notes, often take months or years, cost thousands of dollars and may not lead to available jobs. Skillpoint instead builds its free five-week courses with employers who are hiring now, so participants train for open positions companies need to fill today.Participants earn industry-recognised certifications, visit job sites and train on electrical systems, HVAC equipment and plumbing installations designed to mirror real working conditions. They also receive mentoring and help with job placement.Participants in the programme receive hands-on training, earn industry-recognised certifications, visit job sites and receive mentoring and job placement assistance.According to the organisation, employer partnerships shape every aspect of the curriculum, creating a more direct pathway from training to employment. The results have been significant. The foundation reports that more than three-quarters of graduates secure jobs after completing the programme, while many move into careers that offer greater stability, higher wages and long-term advancement opportunities.The programme comes as Texas continues to face growing demand for skilled workers across critical industries. According to the foundation, many employers struggle to fill essential roles, while adults seeking career advancement often face barriers such as lengthy training periods and high educational costs.The organisation highlighted the story of a graduate named Mariah, who transitioned from security work into an HVAC technician role after completing five weeks of training. She now works as a start-up technician, inspecting and testing newly installed HVAC systems before they reach customers.To meet growing demand, Skillpoint Alliance is expanding its operations in South Austin and New Braunfels. The organisation is further planning to increase the training capacity by updating the families, hiring more instructors and support staff and also running multiple cohorts. The Michael & Susan Dell Foundation claimed that the expansion is aimed at helping more Texans gain access to fast, employer-connected training programmes that can lead to stable careers and improved economic mobility while helping businesses fill critical workforce gaps.
Article Summary: The Michael & Susan Dell Foundation reports that more than three-quarters of graduates secure jobs after completing the programme. The organisation is expanding its operations in South Austin and New Braunfels to meet growing demand. The programme comes as Texas continues to face growing demand for skilled workers across critical industries.

Article Title: PHP runs up to 70% of websites but nonprofit behind it has one full-time employee and 14 part-time contractors
Article Text:
PHP

How PHP coordinates fixes with industry partners

The dual impact of AI

This week, the discovery of two serious vulnerabilities in PHP triggered an emergency global scramble across governments and corporations. The incident exposed the internet’s immense dependence on a three-decade-old, open-source programming language. Yet behind the software that underpins up to 70% of websites worldwide sits an organisation running on scarce resources, a report has said. The nonprofit PHP Foundation, which maintains and safeguards the language, operates on a very thin budget with a minimal team.“We have one full-time staff member (that's me) and 14 mostly part-time contractors,” PHP Foundation Executive Director Elizabeth Barron told news agency Reuters in an email interview. Barron added that the foundation’s board members are entirely unpaid volunteers, with the organisation relying on charitable grants and private donations to keep the lights on.Despite its small headcount, the foundation coordinates directly with major technology firms and external security researchers to triage software bugs and engineer defensive patches. To investigate the latest vulnerabilities and verify the emergency fixes released on Wednesday, the foundation collaborated closely with artificial intelligence (AI) labs OpenAI alongside cybersecurity firms Google-owned Wiz and Calif.While web infrastructure provider Cloudflare reported millions of automated probing attempts following the public disclosure, Barron noted that the foundation has seen no evidence of attackers successfully exploiting the vulnerabilities prior to the announcement, nor on systems that have applied the updates.“We received no further indication from OpenAI, Wiz or Calif, with whom we're working closely on this issue, regarding any issues on patched systems,” Barron stated.The rapid rise of AI has introduced a double-edged sword for the small team maintaining PHP. On one hand, AI tools served as a vital asset with automated models helping researchers uncover the two security flaws, which had quietly lingered in the codebase for over a decade. Barron acknowledged that the technology has also helped software developers work more efficiently.On the other hand, AI has amplified the workload falling on human maintainers. The open-source project is said to be receiving nearly twice as many proposed code modifications compared to last year. Additionally, the number of active contributors reviewing that code has not kept pace with the incoming surge.Evaluating bug reports, pull requests, and automated suggestions still demands “a massive amount of human input and experience” to verify safety and viability.
Article Summary: The nonprofit PHP Foundation, which maintains and safeguards the language, operates on a very thin budget with a minimal team. The foundation coordinates directly with major technology firms and external security researchers to triage software bugs and engineer defensive patches. The rapid rise of AI has introduced a double-edged sword for the small team maintaining PHP.

Article Title: Jeff Bezos' academy opened a free preschool on an Arizona retirement-community campus in 2026; the Glendale school offers meals and learning materials at no cost to eligible families with young childr
Article Text:
Bezos Academy Glendale-Sahuaro Glenn offer free preschool for eligible families

Bringing generations together

Bezos Academy expands its footprint

A new preschool backed by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has opened inside a retirement community in Arizona. The Bezos-backed school promises to offer free arly childhood education. Along with this, the school also provides free meals and leaning materials to eligible families that have young children. The new Bezos Academy Glendale-Sahuaro Glenn campus is located at the Glencroft Center for Modern Aging in Glendale, Arizona, bringing preschool-aged children and senior residents together on the same campus. The school was started in 2026 consists of five classrooms and is designed to serve children aged 3 to 5 from qualifying families. As per Bezos Academy, the campus is located at Glencroft's retirement community and has a planned capacity of 100 students.Fortune reported that families earning up to $132,000 can apply. The cap depends on household size, and the report’s details on this are limited, so families should check the school’s eligibility page. Applications for the 2026-27 school year had to be submitted by April 20 to be included in the lottery.Kresta Horn, head of school at the Glendale campus, said the higher income cap is meant to include children who might otherwise be missed and give them a chance to build important skills before kindergarten.Bezos Academy says it pays for the whole programme. The network covers all operating expenses for its preschools at no cost to families, and it hires, trains and pays its own educators. The Arizona Republic has reported that the programme covers full tuition and meals for eligible children aged 3 to 5. That report described another Glendale campus, so check with the school for what is provided at Sahuaro Glenn, including learning materials. The academy does not offer transportation, but families do not need to live in Glendale to apply.The setting is a central part of the pitch. Glencroft says the preschool is its second major intergenerational initiative in recent years. John Thorhauer, Glencroft’s CEO, said the partnership gives residents a chance to engage with younger generations, sharing their time, knowledge and experience. Glendale Mayor Jerry Weiers said the school creates a setting where students and seniors can learn from each other. One report says about 900 seniors live on the campus. The school’s own website says only that it is grateful to Glencroft for sharing its belief that all children deserve a great start.The Glendale-Sahuaro Glenn school is Bezos Academy's second preschool in the Glendale area, following the opening of the Glendale-Desert Garden Park campus in 2025. According to reports, the new campus is expected to grow to full capacity over the coming years as additional classrooms become operational.The opening comes as education advocates continue to highlight limited preschool access in Arizona and other parts of the United States. Bezos Academy, funded by Bezos' philanthropic initiatives, has steadily expanded its network of tuition-free preschools across multiple states, focusing on communities where affordable early childhood education is in short supply.
Article Summary: New Bezos Academy Glendale-Sahuaro Glenn campus is located at the Glencroft Center for Modern Aging in Glendale, Arizona. The school was started in 2026 consists of five classrooms and is designed to serve children aged 3 to 5 from qualifying families. Families earning up to $132,000 can apply. Bezos Academy says it pays for the whole programme.

Article Title: Apple iPhone Duo scam alert: Fake websites offer 25% discounts to target buyers, Kaspersky warns
Article Text:
iPhone Duo scam alert

Example of a fake website offering to purchase iPhone Duo

Example of a fake multilingual website offering to purchase iPhone Duo

Example of a fake website in Portuguese offering to purchase iPhone Duo

Apple’s first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo, has officially gone on sale on October 23, but scammers are already targeting buyers with fake discounts and preorder offers. Cybersecurity firm Kaspersky has identified fraudulent websites in multiple languages that imitate Apple’s style and use limited-time deals to pressure shoppers into sharing personal information. Some sites promise discounts of up to 25%, while others ask buyers to share their contact details or WhatsApp numbers. Kaspersky has warned buyers to be cautious of unofficial offers as they look to get their hands on the new device.These “offers” are not limited to English-speaking audiences. Kaspersky also identified examples of multilingual pages where users can select their preferred language. In one such case, a fake website showcased various features of the new device and invited users to place a preorder, even allowing them to choose the currency for the purchase. To make the offer appear credible, the site suggested that the user would supposedly be redirected to Apple’s official website — which, in reality, is not the case.Kaspersky researchers also uncovered a fraudulent offer aimed at Portuguese-speaking users. In this instance, the scammers tried to move the conversation to a messaging app from the outset, asking the victim to share the phone number linked to their WhatsApp account as well as their email address in order to check product availability.This tactic not only exposes the victim’s contact information, but also leaves them more vulnerable to further social engineering.“Scammers move fast when a flagship device hits the market, because hype creates urgency and urgency lowers caution. These campaigns are designed to look credible, then push the target into a private exchange before they have time to verify anything. For fraudsters, a flagship buyer is a high-value mark: someone already willing to spend big and therefore more likely to share personal or payment-related details. That is exactly why unofficial discounts, preorders, or ‘availability checks’ should be treated as red flags,” says Olga Altukhova, Senior Web Content Analyst at Kaspersky.To shop for a new device without worrying about cyber threats, Kaspersky recommends that users:•Always purchase new products through official and reputable stores to avoid falling victim to fraudulent offers.•Check the authenticity of websites before entering personal data. Double-check URL formats and organizations name spellings.•Use a reliable security solution that detects fraudulent stores and blocks phishing links. To ensure advanced protection against increasingly complex cyber threats, Kaspersky actively amplifies its consumer solutions with AI-powered scam protection – a unified suite of technologies that combines machine learning-based anti-phishing algorithms, real-time behavior monitoring, accompanied by Data Leak and Identity Theft checkers. In 2025, Kaspersky Premium received the "Approved" certification in Fake Shops Detection test by the leading testing lab AV-Comparatives.•Secure your payment information. Use dedicated virtual cards or a dedicated payment service for online purchases to avoid exposing your credit card or bank account information. Store your credentials and financial data in a password manager for secure auto-fill and cross-device synchronization.•Enable multi-factor authentication and monitor accounts: Activate 2FA on IDs and financial apps and regularly review statements for unauthorized activity.
Article Summary: Kaspersky has identified fraudulent websites in multiple languages that imitate Apple’s style. Some sites promise discounts of up to 25%, while others ask buyers to share their contact details or WhatsApp numbers. Kaspersky warns buyers to be cautious of unofficial offers as they look to get their hands on the new device.

Article Title: Meet Ellianna Gu, the Salt Lake City eighth-grader who tested ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini on 84 teen emotional scenarios and found their replies often lacked empathy
Article Text:
Image credit: YouTube

“Bot-tling up Emotions: How AI Chatbots Interpret and Respond to Emotionally Challenging Scenarios,”

“In a previous project conducted by Stanford, it was found that at times, AI chatbots can lack effectiveness and can have dangerous responses,” G

How Ellianna Gu tested the three chatbots

What the results showed

“I think that the human brain is really fascinating and I would love to learn more about it,”

“I also want to help people, especially those suffering from life-altering conditions such as Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, and Huntington’s disease.”

A teenager has tested AI chatbots' ability to handle teenage emotions. Ellianna Gu, an eighth-grader from Utah's Salt Lake City, examined responses from OpenAI ’s ChatGPT, Anthropic’s Claude, and Google Gemini. She chose this test after learning that some teenagers were turning to these services for friendship and emotional support. Her project used 84 scenarios involving academic stress, social anxiety, friendship problems, family conflict, loneliness, anger and sadness. Gu found that the chatbots generally produced clear and structured answers, but their replies did not display much empathy. Their performance also changed depending on whether a scenario was written formally or with slang, indicating that writing style could affect the support a teenager received.The project, titledmade Gu a finalist in the 2026 Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge. She developed the study after reading earlier research that raised concerns about how chatbots respond to people seeking emotional support.u said.Gu first used AI to create realistic situations based on seven types of emotional challenges commonly faced by teenagers. She varied the language in the prompts, including both slang and more formal writing, before submitting all 84 scenarios to ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini.She then evaluated the replies using four criteria: empathy, clarity, problem-solving and helpfulness. Most categories were scored on a scale of one to three, while empathy was rated on a scale of one to four.Gu assessed the answers manually and also used AI to analyse them. This allowed her to compare the chatbots’ responses using both human judgment and an automated evaluation.The three chatbots generally provided organised and understandable responses. However, Gu found that their answers often lacked empathy, an important quality when responding to a teenager discussing loneliness, anxiety or another emotional concern. The systems also reacted differently depending on how a prompt was written. A scenario expressed through slang could produce a different response than one describing the same problem in formal language.Their effectiveness scores were also limited. According to the project summary, among the three services, only Claude received a score of three for effectiveness. Outside the competition, Gu plays the piano and clarinet and hopes to become a neurologist.she said.
Article Summary: Ellianna Gu, an eighth-grader from Utah's Salt Lake City, examined responses from OpenAI ’s ChatGPT, Anthropic’s Claude, and Google Gemini. She chose this test after learning that some teenagers were turning to these services for friendship and emotional support. Gu found that the chatbots generally produced clear and structured answers, but their replies did not display much empathy.

Article Title: Jeff Bezos’s parents invested $245,573 in Amazon when it was an uncertain online bookstore; that early family investment is worth billions today as the company’s valuation passes $2 trillion
Article Text:
Jeff Bezos’s parents’ risky bet on an unfamiliar business

Jeff Bezos with his parents; mother Jackie Bezos and his Stepfather & Adoptive Father Miguel Bezos

From a small online bookstore to a public company

How the family's investment grew

Amazon's growth transformed the original gamble

The family continued to support education and young people

A decision made before Amazon's success was clear

Also See:

When Jeff Bezos decided to leave his secure job in 1994 to build an online bookstore, he was pursuing an idea that many people struggled to understand. The internet was still unfamiliar to most investors and the future of online shopping remained uncertain. His parents, Jackie and Mike Bezos, nevertheless backed him with $245,573 from their savings in 1995. Bezos later recalled that he warned them they could lose their money. They invested anyway because they believed in their son. Nearly three decades later, Amazon has grown from a small internet bookseller into a global technology and retail giant. The family's early decision has since become one of the most remarkable investment stories linked to the company's rise.The idea for Amazon came to Bezos in 1994 while he was working at an investment firm in New York. He saw the rapid growth of the internet as an opportunity to create a bookstore with a catalogue far larger than any physical shop could accommodate.Bezos decided to leave his job and pursue the idea in Seattle. His parents provided most of the initial start-up capital, putting a substantial portion of their life savings into a business they did not fully understand.In his July 2020 testimony before the US House Judiciary Committee, Bezos said he had told his parents there was a 70% chance they would lose their investment. He explained that they were not necessarily betting on the concept of an online bookstore. They were betting on him.The decision came at a time when convincing investors to back an internet business was difficult. Bezos said he attended more than 50 meetings while trying to raise $1 million. One question repeatedly came up during those discussions: what was the internet.Amazon opened its online store in 1995. The business initially focused on books because the internet offered a way to display a vast selection without the physical limitations of a traditional shop.The response surprised Bezos. In a later account of Amazon's early days, he recalled receiving orders from customers across all 50 US states and 45 countries soon after the store opened.Amazon went public in May 1997 at $18 per share. The initial public offering raised approximately $54 million and gave the company additional capital to expand its operations.Its future was far from secure, however. Amazon recorded cumulative losses of nearly $3 billion between its founding and the end of 2001. It did not report a profitable quarter until the final three months of that year.The company also faced scepticism during the dot-com bubble. Its share price reached $116 at the height of the internet boom before falling to $6 after the bubble burst. Bezos recalled that commentators questioned whether Amazon could survive.The $245,573 investment came in Amazon’s early years, before the company went public. Mike Bezos bought 582,528 shares in February 1995, while Jackie Bezos bought another 847,716 shares in July that year.As Amazon grew from an online bookstore into a global retail and cloud computing giant, its share value increased significantly. The company’s growth turned the family’s early investment into a potentially enormous fortune.The family also donated some of its Amazon shares to the Bezos Family Foundation. According to a 2018 Los Angeles Times report, Jackie and Mike Bezos donated 595,027 shares to the foundation between 2001 and 2016.The exact value of the shares they still hold is not publicly known. A September 2026 Fortune report estimated that Mike Bezos’s remaining stake could be worth about $51.7 billion if he still holds the shares not accounted for by those donations. This is an estimate, not a confirmed figure.Amazon's rise was not driven by online retail alone. Over time, it expanded into cloud computing, digital advertising, streaming, logistics and other technology services.One of its most consequential developments was Amazon Web Services. Bezos said in his congressional testimony that some observers initially viewed cloud computing as a distraction from the company's retail business. AWS eventually became a major part of Amazon's operations.The company also expanded its marketplace by allowing independent sellers to offer products alongside Amazon's own inventory. Bezos said third-party sellers accounted for approximately 60% of physical product sales on Amazon at the time of his 2020 testimony.Jackie and Mike Bezos established the Bezos Family Foundation in 2000 with their children and their spouses. The foundation has focused largely on education and child development, supporting research and programmes designed to help young people.The family's donations of Amazon shares helped channel part of its wealth towards philanthropic work. The foundation's activities provide another dimension to the investment story, connecting the family's early financial support for Bezos with its later efforts to fund educational initiatives.The story of the Bezos family's investment is striking because the outcome was not obvious when the money changed hands. In 1995, Amazon was a young business built around a new way of selling books. Its founder had left a secure job, investors were still learning about the internet and the company had years of financial challenges ahead.Jackie and Mike Bezos accepted the possibility of losing a substantial portion of their savings because they believed in their son. Amazon's eventual growth turned that decision into a landmark example of early backing for a successful technology company.
Article Summary: Jeff Bezos decided to leave his job in 1994 to build an online bookstore. His parents, Jackie and Mike Bezos, invested $245,573 from their savings in 1995. Bezos later recalled that he warned them they could lose their money. They invested anyway because they believed in their son. Nearly three decades later, Amazon has grown from a small internet bookseller into a global technology and retail giant.

Article Title: France protests: Hours after looting in showrooms, listings for luxury items pop-up on Vinted, Amazon and other online marketplaces
Article Text:
French government summons major e-commerce platforms

How stolen goods rapidly were listed online

Amid the unrest that swept across France this week, more than 3,000 retail locations were damaged or looted, Commerce Minister Serge Papin has said. High-end boutiques in Paris’s central Les Halles commercial district, including flagship outlets for Hermès, Louis Vuitton, and The North Face, were among the hardest hit. Now a report has claimed that just hours after storefronts were ransacked, suspicious listings featuring designer handbags, high-end skincare sets and luxury cosmetics began surfacing across leading digital marketplaces, triggering alarm over the mass online fencing of stolen merchandise.Faced with a rapid influx of suspected stolen goods, Papin and digital minister Anne Le Hénanff intervened, convening an urgent virtual conference with top executives from Vinted, French secondhand platform Leboncoin, Amazon, eBay, Meta and TikTok to demand the swift removal of all illicit listings.Secondhand marketplace Vinted confirmed it has enacted emergency safeguards to suppress fraudulent product drops.“The sale of stolen goods, or soliciting them, is strictly prohibited on Vinted, and we have zero tolerance for it. We are actively collaborating with law enforcement and the French authorities, and we continually adapt our processes to detect and counter emerging risks and malicious behaviour,” a Vinted spokesperson told Fortune.The platform noted that the volume of designer merchandise appeared abnormal almost immediately. A Vinted spokesperson previously told trade publication RetailDetail that the platform detected a “clear spike in listings for luxury items” that rarely ever circulate in such high concentrations.E-commerce platform eBay also reaffirmed its ban on stolen merchandise, emphasising that it deploys algorithmic filters and specialised human investigative units to detect suspect merchant accounts and coordinate with law enforcement.According to the report, for criminal operators, high-end cosmetics, luxury accessories, fragrances and portable electronics represent prime targets: they are compact, simple to photograph, command immediate consumer demand and can be liquidated quickly.“Looted items are often sold quickly, in bulk and below market price, and the proceeds move through payment accounts that are themselves a fraud problem,” explained Serpil Hall, strategic advisor at Datos Insights specialising in financial crime.Addressing the unrest, French President Emmanuel Macron issued a warning that authorities would identify and prosecute all looters. Under French criminal law, possessing, handling, or selling stolen goods carries severe penalties: up to five years in prison and fines reaching €375,000 ($420,000).
Article Summary: French government summons major e-commerce platforms over stolen goods listings. High-end boutiques in Paris’s central Les Halles commercial district, including flagship outlets for Hermès, Louis Vuitton, and The North Face, were among the hardest hit. Vinted confirmed it has enacted emergency safeguards to suppress fraudulent product drops.

Article Title: As Tesla presses accelerator on the product that Elon Musk predicted 80% of the company's value will come from; costs jump and profit falls 43%
Article Text:
Optimus production comes to Fremont

Elon Musk 'admits' ride will be bumpy

Tesla CEO Elon Musk has predicted that Optimus robots will eventually make up for more than three-quarters of the automaker’s value. In a post on X, formerly Twitter, in September 2025, Tesla CEO wrote, "~80% of Tesla’s value will be Optimus. ” And this was not the first time that Musk made an upbeat prediction on Optimus robots. Ever since Tesla revealed that it was working on a humanoid robot known as Optimus in 2021, Musk has spent years making the case that Tesla is really an AI and robotics company.Analysts see his attention move decisively to the AI parts of the company, which includes projects like Optimus robot and fully autonomous robotaxis. In mid-2024, at Tesla's annual shareholder meeting, CEO Musk had told shareholders that humanoid robots could lift the company’s market cap to $25 trillion at an unspecified future date. Musk said that Optimus could be the catalyst for lifting Tesla’s market cap to $25 trillion someday. Musk, however, didn’t provide a time frame for reaching $25 trillion.This week, Tesla announced that the company has started production of its Optimus humanoid robot at its factory in Fremont, California, a manufacturing space once dedicated to making electric vehicles (EVs). The company announced the same in a letter to shareholders."Optimus production began in Fremont on our high-volume lines. The bots coming off this line are the first production-quality bots that we have manufactured. While we will continue to iterate on the hardware and manufacturing process, we have proven that the current manufacturing process for Optimus is suitable for a commercial product," reads the letter.Tesla made the Optimus production announcement during its third-quarter results that saw the company reporting 16% year-over-year decline in revenue from its solar and energy storage business to $2.8 billion. There was some positive revenue growth in its services business, a category that includes customer subscriptions to its Full Self-Driving advanced driver-assistance software. Tesla’s services business grew 33% year-over-year, bringing in $4.6 billion and accounting for a record $734 million in gross profit for the quarter.That forward-looking development wasn’t, however, enough to lift the company’s third-quarter earnings. Tesla reported $787 million in net income, a 43% drop from the same period in 2025, when it earned $1.37 billion. According to analysts, none of the revenue gain was enough to outpace Tesla’s spending on artificial intelligence projects and its Optimus robot, which is said to have taken a big bite out of profits.On a conference call, Musk said that he considers Optimus production as "early" right now and that the ramp will be slow and "somewhat bumpy because it is such a radically new product." He nonetheless claimed that Tesla will be able to make 20,000 of them per week by the end of 2027. “There’s still some things we need to tweak about the design, because you need to deliver a robot that is safe and reliable and has a long duration, so it can’t, like, wear out after a month,” he said. “And there’s still quite a lot of work to do with regard to the AI and the robot for it to be truly useful for open-ended tasks,” he added.
Article Summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk has predicted that Optimus robots will eventually make up for more than three-quarters of the automaker's value. In mid-2024, Musk told shareholders that humanoid robots could lift the company’s market cap to $25 trillion at an unspecified future date. Tesla announced that the company has started production of its Optimus humanoid robot at its factory.

Article Title: Google co-founder Larry Page is the richest tech titan to leave California ahead of Billionaire's tax vote: How his exit may dent state’s $100 billion tax target
Article Text:
Moving entities to Delaware and buying big in Miami

The $29 billion dent in Prop 40’s target

With Californians set to vote in just a few weeks on Proposition 40 – a measure proposing a one-time 5% wealth tax on the state's billionaires – Google co-founder Larry Page has emerged as the wealthiest tech titan to sever ties with the state should the measure pass. His departure is likely to deal a significant blow to California's revenue projections as he will be the richest techie to leave the state. The initiative specifically targets billionaires who were state residents as of January 1, 2026. While a few prominent executives, such as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, have stated they are "perfectly fine" with the proposal, multiple ultra-wealthy residents chose to exit before the January deadline.Chief among them is the 53-year-old Page. Holding an estimated net worth of around $260 billion, Page had deep roots in California spanning decades, Fortune reported, adding that had he remained a California resident past the cutoff date, he would have owed an estimated $15 billion under the one-time tax levy.State filings have revealed that Page began unwinding his operational and personal presence in California late last year.According to an analysis of corporate records reported by Fortune, Page’s family office, Koop, was transferred out of California and officially incorporated in Delaware in late December. Multiple associated entities, including Flu Lab LLC, One Aero and Oceankind, followed the same route, moving their registrations from California to Delaware during the same month.Simultaneously, Page redirected significant capital toward luxury real estate on the East Coast. The Wall Street Journal reported that Page acquired two premier estates in Miami for a combined $173.4 million, which includes Coconut Grove Estate ($101.5 million, 11,855-square-foot property) and a neighboring parcel purchased for $71.9 million.The departures of top-tier billionaires have already weakened the potential financial yield of the ballot measure. Prop 40 was projected to generate roughly $100 billion for the state. However, according to an estimate by Fortune, just four departed tech leaders – Larry Page, Sergey Brin, Peter Thiel and former Uber CEO Travis Kalanick – would have collectively owed approximately $29 billion. Their relocations before the residency cutoff mean the state has effectively lost out on more than a quarter of the measure's total projected revenue pool before ballots are even counted.Elon Musk, the richest person in the world, moved to Texas in 2020. Meanwhile, Jeff Bezos who recently but briefly secured the second richest person spot, departed Seattle for Miami in late 2023, eventually selling his Hunts Point home for a record $63 million to live in a $237 million Miami compound with his wife, Lauren Sánchez Bezos.
Article Summary: Google co-founder Larry Page is the wealthiest tech titan to sever ties with the state should the measure pass. His departure is likely to deal a significant blow to California's revenue projections. The initiative specifically targets billionaires who were state residents as of January 1, 2026.

Article Title: Google changes its privacy policy: Your Gmail, Photos data may now be used for ads; what it means for you
Article Text:
Personal Intelligence is what links your Gmail to Google ads

Turning off personalised ads alone won’t stop Gmail data use

Google has reworked a long-standing promise about your inbox. Its updated privacy policy, effective October 16, now allows content from Gmail, Google Photos and Drive to shape the ads you see, as long as you have shared that data with other Google services. The change was first spotted by Android Authority.Until now, the policy carried a plain line saying Google does not show personalised ads based on your Drive, Gmail or Photos content. That line is still there, but it now ends with a qualifier: "unless you choose to make data from these services available to other Google services that support personalized ads." In practice, this covers anyone who has turned on Personal Intelligence, the feature that lets Gemini and AI Mode in Search read from your personal apps.Google pitches Personal Intelligence as a convenience. Ask Search for dinner spots near your hotel, and it can pull the booking from Gmail and suggest restaurants close by. Once connected, that access stretches beyond AI Mode to Discover, Maps, Shopping, Flights, Hotels, Translate and News. The Gemini app has no ads for now, but AI search results already carry sponsored content, and that is where the two meet.Google maintains the feature is entirely opt-in. In a statement, the company said ads will stay relevant to your query, the context of the response and your interests, and "will not be based directly on your Gmail inbox or Photos library."Advertisers cannot see your emails or photos, and your name and email address are not shared with them. Ads built on sensitive categories such as health, religion, race or sexual orientation are still ruled out.Search, however, can still work with summaries and inferences drawn from your emails and photos, and those can feed into what you are shown. Switching off personalised ads in My Ad Center does not stop connected-app data from being used for AI personalisation either.To cut the link, open your Google Account and go to Data & privacy, then Personalisation settings. Select Manage Personalized Recommendations in Search Services, find Connected Content Apps under Additional Personal Intelligence, and disconnect Google Workspace and Google Photos. You can also switch off Personalized Recommendations altogether from the Search Services Personalization page.There is one more step. As Android Authority points out, disconnecting an app does not erase what Google has already stored in Search Services History, even if you delete the original email or photo. That has to be cleared separately from My Activity, or the old data stays tied to your account.
Article Summary: Google has updated its privacy policy to allow personalised ads based on Gmail, Google Photos and Drive content. The change, effective October 16, covers anyone who has turned on Personal Intelligence. Personal Intelligence is what links your Gmail to Google ads. Google maintains the feature is entirely opt-in.

Article Title: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu says India must 'build, build and build' to earn global respect: Until India develops, we will …
Article Text:
Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu

Why Sridhar Vembu says India must focus on building

Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu has called on India to focus on developing its own talent, businesses and technology, saying the country will earn true respect globally by building on the abilities of its people. His remarks came in response to American investor and podcaster Eric Weinstein, who raised concerns about growing hostility towards India, Indians, Hindus and Indian-Americans on social media. In a post on X, Vembu said India should respond to racism by focusing on development rather than hatred. He also said the country's progress should not depend on which political side is in power.“Until India develops, based on the talents of our own people, we will not find true respect in the world, no matter whether right, left or center is in charge anywhere,” Sridhar Vembu wrote.Eric Weinstein, an American investor and mathematician, wrote on X that he was seeing growing hatred towards India and its people without any reason. “Seeing a lot of growing raw hatred against India, Indians, Hindus, Indian-Americans, etc. for no reason.Would be happy to have anyone who feels that hatred quietly unfollow me. Simple. Clean. Thanks in advance,” he wrote.His post drew attention to the hostility faced by Indians and people of Indian origin, including those living in the United States.Responding to Weinstein, Sridhar Vembu said India needs to develop through the talent of its own people to gain genuine respect around the world.“Until India develops, based on the talents of our own people, we will not find true respect in the world, no matter whether right, left or center is in charge anywhere,” he wrote. Vembu also addressed racist remarks that questioned why Indians move abroad if India has talented people. He said such comments should encourage the country to build stronger businesses and institutions rather than respond with hatred.“The racist shows us a mirror and asks: "if your nation is smart, why do you want to come here". I do not hate him, I want to respond by building.”He added that he holds the same view towards Indians who believe the country will never develop. “Some Indians agree with the racist and think India will never develop. I do not hate them either, I want to respond by building.”Vembu said belief in the possibility of progress was important for building successful companies and nations. “Companies and nations are built by people who believe it can be done.”He ended his post with a call for greater focus on development and building India's capabilities. “The urgent national priority is to build, build and build.”
Article Summary: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu calls on India to focus on developing its own talent, businesses and technology. His remarks came in response to American investor and podcaster Eric Weinstein, who raised concerns about growing hostility towards India, Indians, Hindus and Indian-Americans on social media.

Article Title: US military has a 'dog problem' that goes to Europe Palmer Luckey and Ben Lamm have a plan to solve it: Genetically engineered...
Article Text:
Representative image

America's dependence on European military dogs

How the plan works

Gene editing aimed at healthier service animals

Anduril brings the hardware

A subscription model for military dogs

The 'Captain America dog program'

The US military relies heavily on working dogs for missions ranging from explosives detection to security operations, but according to a new Fortune report, America is facing a growing shortage of suitable military canines. Now, a new defence technology startup backed by prominent Silicon Valley investors believes it has a solution: genetically engineered, cloned military dogs equipped with advanced protective gear and integrated with battlefield technologies. As per the Fortune report, Warhound, a new Texas-based defence startup conceived by Anduril founder Palmer Luckey and Colossal Biosciences CEO Ben Lamm, has emerged from stealth mode with a $200 million seed funding round. The company aims to use cloning and gene-editing technologies to create healthier, more capable working dogs while reducing the U.S. military's dependence on European breeders.According to the report, more than 80% of U.S. military working dogs are currently sourced from Europe. The Pentagon's Military Working Dog Program operates more than 2,200 dog teams, but finding suitable animals has become increasingly difficult.Lamm told Fortune that the United States is competing with foreign governments, including China and Russia, to acquire top-quality dogs from a limited pool of overseas breeders. The challenge is compounded by the fact that less than half of the dogs purchased ultimately qualify for military service after completing a lengthy training and evaluation process.As a result, the military reportedly needs to purchase and train around 200 dogs to eventually field 100 operational working animals, significantly increasing costs and logistical challenges.Lamm's confidence in the project stems from technology developed at Colossal Biosciences, the company known for its high-profile de-extinction efforts. Earlier this year, Colossal announced the creation of animals carrying genetic traits inspired by the extinct dire wolf through gene-editing and cloning techniques.Lamm described the approach in stages. Warhound will find top dogs that have finished training and bank their genetic material. It will then clone those proven animals, though Lamm acknowledged that training and environment will always influence performance. In parallel, the company will pursue targeted gene edits. The first group of dogs has already been banked and is being edited, and Lamm expects to deliver the first dogs in about two years.Edits will first aim to screen out known harmful variants linked to muscle degeneration and other inherited diseases, so that no dog enters service carrying markers for common career-ending conditions. Lamm said the company is still deciding which other traits are scientifically and responsibly actionable, but is planning future genetic enhancements to improve performance."The first group of dogs has already been biobanked and is being edited now," Lamm told Fortune, adding that the company expects its first dogs to be delivered within approximately two years.Warhound says its initial focus will be eliminating known genetic conditions linked to issues such as muscle degeneration and other inherited diseases that can prematurely end a dog's military career. Lamm said the company is still determining which additional characteristics can be responsibly enhanced through biotechnology, but acknowledged that Warhound is considering future genetic modifications to improve performance beyond current standards.The company argues that reducing genetic health risks could increase the number of dogs capable of successfully completing demanding military training programmes.While Colossal's technology forms the biological foundation of the project, Luckey's defence company Anduril will contribute the equipment layer. Warhound plans to equip dogs with protective technologies including body armour, eye and hearing protection, and integration with Anduril's Eagle Eye situational awareness platform. The company describes these systems as "cybernetic augments" designed to allow dogs, handlers and autonomous systems to operate as a coordinated team.Despite the futuristic vision, Lamm rejected suggestions that the programme is a stepping stone toward robotic replacements. "No machine today matches a dog's nose or its judgment in complex environments," he said.Warhound has not yet secured official customers and has not disclosed pricing. However, the company is reportedly exploring a "Canine-as-a-Service" model in which government agencies would pay for a continuous supply of trained and supported working dogs rather than purchasing individual animals.The approach mirrors subscription-based procurement models increasingly used across the defence technology sector. The startup's investors include In-Q-Tel, Sequoia Capital, ARK Invest, Franklin Templeton, 8VC, Breyer Capital, Lux Capital and several other venture firms.Lamm described the concept as something akin to a "Captain America dog program," referencing the comic-book super-soldier project that transformed Steve Rogers into Captain America. According to Lamm, the idea emerged during a conversation with Luckey at entrepreneur Peter Diamandis' Moonshots Summit, where the two discussed military dog shortages, high training failure rates and growing procurement costs.Although Luckey helped develop the concept, Lamm stressed that Warhound operates independently. Former Pentagon Chief Data Officer David Spirk, a Marine veteran with extensive experience in defence and intelligence organisations, has been appointed CEO and will lead the company as it seeks to turn biotechnology research into field-ready military capabilities. Luckey summed up the project's mission in a statement to Fortune: "Man's best friend deserves man's best tech. "
Article Summary: Texas-based defence startup Warhound has emerged from stealth mode with a $200 million seed funding round. The company aims to use cloning and gene-editing technologies to create healthier, more capable working dogs. Warhound plans to equip dogs with protective technologies including body armour, eye and hearing protection, and integration with Anduril's Eagle Eye situational awareness platform.

Article Title: Engineer sues datacenter developer Nscale as it gets ready for listing on New York stock exchange; claims fired over letter to HR complaining over …
Article Text:
Nscale

Lawsuit comes at Nscale gets ready for NYSE listing

United Kingdom-based artificial intelligence infrastructure provider Nscale is facing a wrongful dismissal lawsuit in Norway. According to a report in Bloomberg, a former data center engineer has alleged in a lawsuit that the UK-based datacenter developer has utilized an illegal subcontracting setup. The lawsuit, filed on October 16 in the Sr-Rogaland District Court and backed by local trade unions, names both Nscale and staffing subcontractor CloudBrothers as defendants.According to the complaint reviewed by Bloomberg, the engineer claims that while he was placed at Nscale’s Stavanger facility through CloudBrothers, Nscale acted as his de facto employer by directly dictating his day-to-day duties and shift schedules. Under Norwegian labor law, subcontracting arrangements require staffing companies to manage personnel independently; end clients that treat subcontracted personnel as direct extensions of their own workforce are legally required to grant them full employee rights and compensation.The engineer alleges his June dismissal came as retaliation after he objected to employment practices at the facility. Tensions surfaced when CloudBrothers human resources reportedly told employees that two weeks of holiday pay would be withheld if vacation requests were submitted late."You cannot deduct our worked salary," the engineer replied in an email copying the entire team, the complaint states.After subsequently raising concerns regarding pay and labor conditions with the Norwegian Labor Inspection Authority, the engineer was terminated. While CloudBrothers stated the dismissal was prompted by repeated confidentiality breaches, the suit claims the firing was retaliatory. The engineer is seeking financial compensation, damages, and a formal judicial declaration recognizing him as an official Nscale employee.Nscale and CloudBrothers did not immediately respond to requests for comment from Bloomberg. Nscale previously confirmed it had cut ties in Stavanger with another contractor, Technimove, which had placed staff through CloudBrothers.The legal action underscores the mounting operational strains confronting Nscale as it scrambles to construct facilities to fulfill more than $100 billion in contractual obligations ahead of a planned initial public offering (IPO) in New York Stock Exchange.Nscale, which rents out computing power for training and running AI models, filed for its IPO in September. According to its IPO filing, it had $103.4 billion in signed and active contracts at the end of August this year. The company reportedly plans to list on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker NSCL and raise up to $3bn.Norway serves as a key pillar in Nscale's European roadmap, driven by access to competitive hydropower. Backed by major shareholder Aker AS, the company operates across sites in Stavanger, Glomfjord, Oslo, and Narvik. However, rapid scaling has brought complications; There have been reports of equipment malfunctions, cooling leaks, and safety issues at Nscale's Glomfjord location.Adding to the Nscale's woes, Microsoft has reportedly pulled out of a deal to be the main tenant at the company's planned data centre in Loughton, Essex. The software giant Microsoft reportedly made the decision to exit after grid operators said that they do not expect to supply power to the site until the 2030s.
Article Summary: UK-based artificial intelligence infrastructure provider Nscale is facing a wrongful dismissal lawsuit in Norway. A former data center engineer has alleged in a lawsuit that the UK-based datacenter developer has utilized an illegal subcontracting setup. The lawsuit, filed on October 16 in the Sr-Rogaland District Court, names both Nscale and staffing subcontractor CloudBrothers as defendants.

Article Title: Airbnb announces a new ban that goes into effect starting November 20, tells hosts across the world that you cannot make guests complete ...
Article Text:
What Airbnb's new policy says

Airbnb hosts react to the new restrictions

Airbnb also restricts separate contracts

What the changes mean for cleaning fees

Airbnb is introducing new rules for hosts and guests. These new rules restrict the checkout tasks hosts can require guests to complete. The policy, which applies to bookings made on or after November 20, prohibits hosts from asking guests to do cleaning duties typically handled by professional cleaners. These include stripping beds, taking rubbish offsite and washing and putting away dishes.The company has also said hosts cannot bypass the restrictions by moving such instructions to other sections of their listings or providing printed checkout lists. The announcement has triggered criticism from some hosts, who argue that the changes limit their ability to protect their properties, while some travellers have welcomed the move amid longstanding complaints about cleaning fees and checkout chores.According to a WIRED report, Airbnb emailed hosts this week to inform them of the changes. The updated rules prohibit hosts from requiring guests to do tasks a cleaner would normally perform.Airbnb says hosts can still make reasonable demands, such as asking visitors to put dirty dishes in the washbasin. Other authorised directives might require guests to dispose of their trash in bear-proof containers or to save water in places with drought-related limitations.However, hosts cannot require guests to strip beds, wash and put away dishes or take rubbish offsite as a condition of checkout.Airbnb has also restricted attempts to circumvent the rules by placing cleaning instructions in a listing's “Requests” section. In an example shared in a Facebook group for hosts, a user claimed the platform prevented them from saving checkout instructions that included washing dishes, moving dirty towels to a laundry room and taking rubbish to a dumpster.The interface reportedly displayed a message stating, "Guests shouldn't be asked to do this task."Some property owners have criticised the announcement, saying the changes limit their ability to set expectations for guests and protect their homes.“As hosts, we have a responsibility to protect our investments, our homes, and, in many cases, our personal living spaces. The problem is that Airbnb increasingly expects hosts to accept the risks while limiting our ability to protect ourselves,” one person wrote in Airbnb’s official host forum.Another host, posting on Reddit, compared the platform’s approach to an abusive relationship, while some users talked about decluttering their rental kitchens or rethinking hosting altogether.Some hosts have also suggested raising rental prices or temporarily withdrawing listings to protest the changes.A third host took to a Facebook group to write, “Even if we all unlist our properties for just a day or two, we can send a powerful message. Airbnb built its empire on OUR properties. It’s time we reminded them who actually holds the power.”But the policy changes go beyond cleaning instructions. Starting November 20, Airbnb will also ban hosts from forcing guests to sign separate contracts, with certain exceptions.These include situations involving local legal requirements, longer stays or access to optional amenities, such as golf cart rentals. Hosts must disclose applicable requirements in the designated section of their listings.Airbnb has also clarified that it does not enforce these contracts. Hosts who breach the new rules could receive warnings, have their listings removed or, in severe cases, be banned from the platform.The company already has ground rules requiring guests to treat properties responsibly, dispose of rubbish properly and avoid leaving dirty dishes that could become a health concern.The new policy comes amid longstanding complaints from travellers about paying cleaning fees and still being asked to complete checkout chores.Airbnb says cleaning fees cover standard turnover work, including laundry and vacuuming. Hosts cannot charge guests additional fees for failing to complete specific cleaning or checkout tasks, although they can still leave reviews based on cleanliness.The platform’s guest program, AirCover, also covers some types of guest-caused property damage, with eligible claims covered up to $3 million. The program can also cover other cleaning costs, such as removing smoke odours or cleaning up pet accidents.Some hosts say the restrictions could make it harder to keep their properties up to snuff, but travellers are embracing fewer chores, especially as cleaning fees are baked into the price of a reservation.The changes will therefore affect how hosts communicate checkout expectations, with Airbnb drawing a clearer distinction between reasonable requests and cleaning work that guests cannot be required to perform.
Article Summary: Airbnb is introducing new rules for hosts and guests. These new rules restrict the checkout tasks hosts can require guests to complete. The policy, which applies to bookings made on or after November 20, prohibits hosts from asking guests to do cleaning duties. These include stripping beds, taking rubbish offsite and washing and putting away dishes.

Article Title: Experts warn wave of AI-discovered flaws to trigger fresh disruptions in coming months
Article Text:
Weeklong disclosures and ‘fire drills’

Rapid breakthroughs in artificial intelligence (AI) have begun unearthing a stream of hidden software bugs, and cybersecurity leaders warn that the discoveries are certain to trigger waves of disruption in the months ahead. The forecast follows a turbulent week where government agencies and public institutions across Europe, Asia and other regions took government and public portals offline to guard against newly surfaced vulnerabilities in PHP, an open-source programming language that underpins a vast swath of the modern web. Citing multiple cybersecurity professionals, news agency Reuters reported that the episode is just the beginning.Matthew Prince, CEO of cloud and infrastructure giant Cloudflare, confirmed that he is tracking “a bunch of additional severe vulnerabilities that are present in other pieces of critical software.” He cautioned that the sector faces an intense operational stretch as algorithmic tools scour the foundational code of the internet for long-buried weak spots.“I think we’re going to have a couple years where every single week it’s going to feel like the sky is falling,” Prince was quoted as saying.The emergency scramble around PHP did not occur in isolation. According to VulnCheck researcher Patrick Garrity, it coincided with an already present cycle of security disclosures and infrastructure incidents across the tech landscape. Over the same seven-day window critical vulnerabilities were disclosed in Node.js (a popular alternative to PHP) as well as the streaming media platform Plex.Additionally, security breaches surfaced around AI gateway LiteLLM and modern application hosting platform Railway. Revelations emerged that Indian certifying authority eMudhra had relied on an extraordinarily weak cryptographic key, raising potential safety concerns for web users globally.“If we just saw four or five things like this, this week, I would expect we’re going to see a lot more. I think there’s going to be a lot more fire drills for anything that’s internet exposed,” Garrity noted.Modern software platforms rely on massive, sprawling codebases where overlooked flaws can linger for decades.In the past, discovering a complex vulnerability required specialised manual auditing. Engineering a working digital lockpick typically demanded weeks or months of meticulous reverse-engineering by highly skilled researchers. That delay granted security teams a vital buffer window to write, test, and quietly distribute defensive software patches.AI has upended that balance. Autonomous models can continuously audit millions of lines of code, flagging vulnerabilities in succession and synthesising functional exploit payloads in hours.
Article Summary: cybersecurity leaders warn that the discoveries are certain to trigger waves of disruption in the months ahead. The forecast follows a turbulent week where government agencies and public institutions across Europe, Asia and other regions took government and public portals offline to guard against newly surfaced vulnerabilities in PHP.
