Article Title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang dismisses memory oversupply fears in 2029, says ‘one of the things that is…’
Article Text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang

Tech companies lose over $1 trillion in a week after memory sell-off

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang dismissed concerns over a memory chip glut, saying that a supply surplus is unlikely to materialise by 2029, even as memory stocks tumbled over the past week on fears of cooling artificial intelligence (AI) demand and an increase in RAM production. Speaking to CNBC on the sidelines of Nvidia’s GTC Berlin conference, Huang pushed back against market speculation that the ongoing hardware supercycle is nearing an abrupt end.“One of the things that’s really great about memory is that you can always use more of it,” Huang said, underscoring that High Bandwidth Memory (HBM), which is a specialised form of RAM critical for AI acceleration, will continue to see widespread use for years to come. Huang also highlighted Nvidia's architectural shift toward integrating low-power memory into massive compute clusters.“We’re the first company in the world to put LPDDR memory – what goes into your cell phones – into the world’s data centers, and it’s enabled us to deliver performance that’s twice as energy efficient as anything in the world today, and so we’re going to continue to use abundant amounts of them as well,” he added.The recent sell-off in semiconductor and memory equities followed an October 15 opinion column in a popular South Korean publication warning policymakers in Seoul to prepare for a slowdown in the AI-driven market boom.Citing two industry experts, the article cautioned that the market could see a “flood of new supply” that transforms the sector “into a red ocean” by 2029. The analysts warned that “the supercycle could be over, and the industry could enter a downturn” within the decade.As memory forms an important backbone of Nvidia’s accelerated hardware, any severe oversupply could erode pricing power and compress margins for top global fabricators, including SK Hynix, Samsung Electronics and Micron Technology.The claims also drew attention from Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, who weighed in on social media to note that China “will be making a LOT of RAM in 2028”, after China’s ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) unveiled a new design architecture, sparking fears that the domestic Chinese producer could chip away at the market share commanded by Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron.Asked whether Nvidia would consider sourcing memory products directly from CXMT, Huang signaled a pragmatic approach to the global hardware supply chain.“We’re open-minded. We work with Chinese companies; just about the whole world works with Chinese companies in the supply chain somewhere,” Huang stated, adding, “China is incredible at the fundamental infrastructure technology, and no country collectively is better at manufacturing than China, and so we have to take their capabilities very seriously.”
Article Summary: N Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang dismissed concerns over a memory chip glut, saying that a supply surplus is unlikely to materialise by 2029. Memory stocks tumbled over the past week on fears of cooling artificial intelligence (AI) demand. Huang also highlighted Nvidia's architectural shift toward integrating low-power memory into massive compute clusters.

Article Title: Computer hidden behind a fridge in a hotel room in Japan had been sending lakhs of phishing emails to steal card details since over a year; used hotel Wi-Fi; here's how it was traced
Article Text:
Hidden behind a fridge: How the phishing PC ran

How the hidden PC was traced in Japan hotel

74 smartphones and 10 million Yen in fraudulent purchases

Japanese police have arrested a Chinese couple after a computer, tucked away behind a refrigerator in a Kobe hotel room, was discovered running a massive email scam for more than a year. In this unusual cybercrime case, the hidden machine was connected to the hotel’s public Wi-Fi and sent out an estimated 480,000 phishing emails designed to deceive recipients and steal their credit card credentials.The suspects, identified as 39-year-old Ye Jiafeng and his 39-year-old wife, Shen Qi – both local residents – were taken into custody not only for operating the hidden system but also for allegedly using stolen credit card data to finance high-value shopping sprees, Tom’s Hardware reported (via Hackread). Both individuals now face multiple criminal charges, including computer fraud, trespass and fraudulent obstruction of business.The operation began on May 15, 2025, when Ye hooked up the computer to the hotel’s wireless internet network and concealed it behind a refrigerator in one of the guest rooms. Once secured in place, the machine was managed remotely, removing any need for either suspect to return to the room for physical maintenance.Reportedly, operating quietly from its hiding spot, the computer fired off roughly 4.8 lakh fraudulent messages. When investigators finally seized the unit, they found a database containing around 2.4 million email addresses queued up for future phishing runs. The outgoing messages impersonated legitimate credit card issuers, directing recipients to counterfeit landing pages to harvest payment details and security numbers.The covert setup would likely have continued running unnoticed if an observant recipient had not taken action. After receiving one of the phishing messages, the recipient analysed the email’s technical metadata and spotted the hotel’s IP address. The individual alerted the hotel management, prompting staff to search the premises.Upon finding the computer concealed behind the refrigerator, the hotel reported the device directly to law enforcement authorities. Police investigators are continuing their inquiry to determine whether the couple planned and controlled the operation themselves or acted as ground-level operators for a larger criminal syndicate.Authorities allege that Ye and Shen loaded stolen credit card details onto smartphones to make fraudulent retail purchases across Kobe. A subsequent raid of the couple’s home uncovered a cache of 74 mobile phones. The pair had siphoned roughly 10 million yen (around $63,000) using victims' stolen cards since 2024. Investigators are still trying to determine whether the 74 devices recovered are all their hardware, or whether more phones were used.
Article Summary: Chinese couple arrested in Japan for running massive email scam. PC was hidden behind a refrigerator in a Kobe hotel room for more than a year. It sent out an estimated 480,000 phishing emails designed to steal credit card credentials. Couple also allegedly used stolen credit card data to finance high-value shopping sprees.

Article Title: Bharti Enterprises chairman Sunil Bharti Mittal: Sovereignty is at the centre of Airtel’s cloud strategy
Article Text:
Sunil Bharti Mittal

Bharti Airtel is sharpening its focus on cloud as a strategic growth engine, that can help enterprises migrate, scale and modernise with greater control over their data and digital operations. Airtel Cloud is being positioned not simply as another cloud storage option, but as an India-based infrastructure proposition focused on scale, connectivity, data control and regulated workloads. The platform offers IaaS, PaaS and advanced connectivity, and is designed to enable secure migration, effortless scaling, lower costs and no vendor lock-ins.Sunil Bharti Mittal, founder and chairman, Bharti Enterprises, has identified cloud, AI infrastructure and data centers as central to the company’s next phase of growth. “I would say that AI infrastructure, data centers and cloud services are among the most important opportunities for us.”, he said, speaking at a recent event.“Sovereign cloud is a major area of focus. Every country is becoming increasingly concerned about digital sovereignty and ensuring that its data remains protected within its borders. Airtel and our companies are working intensively to develop our own sovereign cloud capabilities.We intend to serve enterprises, governments and other organisations through these platforms.”, he added.For enterprises navigating digital transformation, the proposition is particularly relevant at a time when organisations are seeking cloud infrastructure that combines performance with data residency and sovereignty. Airtel Cloud is hosted in India and built to serve businesses that need dependable, secure and locally controlled cloud capabilities.In the company’s annual report for FY 2025-26, Sunil Bharti Mittal described Airtel Cloud as one of three clear areas where the company believes it has a competitive advantage.“Over the last few years, we took a calibrated approach to build new growth engines for Airtel. These bold bets yielded strong outcomes and have grown our conviction in three adjacencies where we believe Airtel has a clear right to win – financial services, data centers and Airtel Cloud.”Airtel Cloud’s telco-grade heritage is central to its differentiation. The platform was developed to run Airtel’s own mission-critical digital operations. The built-in-India, built-for-India platform is positioned as India’s first telco-grade cloud platform, enabling enterprises across the country to adopt cloud infrastructure with confidence.Launched in August 2025 by Airtel’s digital subsidiary Xtelify, Airtel Cloud is a sovereign, telco-grade cloud platform designed for Indian enterprises. It was originally developed to support Airtel’s own large-scale digital operations and has been battle-tested to handle 1.4 billion transactions per minute.
Article Summary: Sunil Bharti Mittal has identified cloud, AI infrastructure and data centers as central to the company’s next phase of growth. Airtel Cloud is being positioned as an India-based infrastructure proposition focused on scale, connectivity, data control and regulated workloads.

Article Title: Sigma’s pocket-sized full-frame FP2 launches in India for Rs 2,16,500
Article Text:
Sigma FP2 goes on sale across India on November 11

One switch turns the Sigma FP2 into a cinema camera

Sigma has launched the FP2 in India, a compact full-frame camera priced at Rs 2,16,500 for the body alone. It goes on sale across the country on November 11, and Sigma claims it is the smallest full-frame camera body in the world.The FP2 follows the original fp, which arrived in 2019 as a tiny, box-shaped camera meant to be built up with accessories. The new model keeps that modular idea and pairs it with faster hardware for both stills and video.Inside is a 24.5MP partially stacked CMOS sensor. Sigma says the quicker readout cuts down rolling shutter, the skewed look you get when panning fast on an electronic shutter. Burst shooting reaches about 20fps for up to 200 frames, and autofocus now tracks birds alongside people and animals. There is 70GB of built-in storage next to the SD card slot, so a full card doesn't have to end a shoot. The rear screen tilts 90 degrees up and 45 degrees down, while a dedicated Color button cycles through 13 colour modes.Flip the switch on top and the FP2 reloads its menus, controls and workflow for CINE mode. It records 6K open gate, using the full sensor area so footage can be cropped later for vertical and horizontal platforms.Sigma rates dynamic range at 14.1 stops, with 7 stops of highlight headroom at ISO 1250 and above in 4K full-frame L-Log. ProRes RAW, Leica L-Log, anamorphic desqueeze and 32-bit float audio are all supported. A Director's Viewfinder mode simulates the framing of cinema cameras like the ARRI ALEXA 35 and Sony VENICE 2 and BURANO.Standard 1/4-inch threads let users attach third-party rigs, and Sigma has four new accessories. The EVF-21 viewfinder uses a 5.76M-dot OLED panel, runs off a single USB-C cable and tilts up 90 degrees. The HU-21 hot shoe shares flash communication with OM System and Lumix. There's also the LVF-21 loupe with 2.5x magnification and the BPL-21 base plate for 3/8-inch video gear. Sigma hasn't shared India pricing for these yet.
Article Summary: Sigma FP2 goes on sale across India on November 11 for Rs 2,16,500 for the body alone. It follows the original fp, which arrived in 2019 as a tiny, box-shaped camera meant to be built up with accessories. New model keeps that modular idea and pairs it with faster hardware for both stills and video.
